`auto` uses the private-state order; an explicit path is the exact effective private root, absolute or operator-home-relative, a real directory the operator can write to whatever its owner and mode; it cannot change its own config discovery. The `socket` and `state` subtrees under it are the operator's own, so a root is never shared: the shared trees are `sharedroot`'s.

The site's shared root, holding the `jobs`, `crun`, and `transcripts` trees that `sudo karvi setup shared` creates with group write and setgid: `auto` consults `/opt/karvi/shared`, then `/var/lib/karvi/shared`; `none` consults nothing; a path consults that directory. A tree that exists there is the default of `output.root`, `crun.directory`, or `transcript.root` in place of the one under `basedir`, and a tree the operator cannot create files in is refused.

The scratch directory of the askpass socket and the system transport's ssh configuration. `auto` is the chain `/dev/shm/karvi/<username>` (only when the site's scratch root `/dev/shm/karvi` exists: `sudo karvi setup shared` makes it, and karvi never does), `<basedir>/tmp`, `/tmp/karvi-<uid>`, `/var/tmp/karvi-<uid>`, the first that is a writable real directory, made 0700 in its existing parent; an absolute path replaces the chain.

The directory of the output spools, one file per command in flight whose response has passed `output.spool-threshold-bytes`. `auto` tries `/tmp/karvi-<uid>`, then `/var/tmp/karvi-<uid>`, each made 0700 for the effective uid, a real directory and not a link, probed with one file; an absolute path replaces the list; no candidate writable is `spool_directory_unavailable`, before any device is touched. Not `tempdir`: the scratch is for small, short-lived files and its `auto` chain prefers `/dev/shm`, a tmpfs, while a spool is infrequent and possibly large and must cost disk, never memory; a site that wants both on one volume points both keys at explicit paths there. Resolved and swept at the daemon's start and at every job's admission.

The folder every activity writes its scoreboard in and `karvi watch` reads. `auto` is `/dev/shm/karvi/scoreboards`, every operator's, where the site's scratch root `/dev/shm/karvi` exists (`sudo karvi setup shared` makes it, at 3770 in the operators' group; a missing `scoreboards` is made in the root with its bits), else the private `<basedir>/state/scoreboards`; a shared folder present but not writable by the operator is passed by for the private one with one warning. `karvi watch` reads every place of the chain that exists, the shared folder and the private one. A path (`~` the operator's home, a relative path from the working directory) replaces the chain, used or refused.

The free-space check of every volume an activity writes, read once per volume at admission before any device is contacted: the job's output root, a `crun`'s collection directory, `spooldir`, and a recorded login's transcripts root, grouped by the device behind each path. `auto` (the default) asks each volume for the sum of what the places on it will hold when the job has finished (the output root `output.expected-bytes-per-device` × devices × its copies × `output.reserve-multiplier`, the collection directory one copy, the spool directory the job's width × the largest command limit in the job, `output.max-command-bytes` or a larger `--maxbytes`, the transcripts root nothing) plus `output.min-free-bytes-after-job` once; when the spool's term alone is short but at least one command's limit fits, the job runs narrower with the warning `spool_width_narrowed`, and below that, or short of the other terms, the job is refused with `output_preflight_space` naming the volume's paths and both figures. `always` asks each volume for the floor alone. `never` reads nothing (the directories are still resolved and probed writable). The audit file, the scoreboard directory, and the state root are not checked: their first write lands before any device and they write kilobytes after. Alerting on free space is the site's monitoring, not this check (`docs/SCALE.md`).

Send exactly two ICMP echo probes to each target's selected address before opening its device transport. One reply proceeds with a packet-loss notice; two misses skip the target as `icmp_unreachable` with no transport attempt. `--ping` and `--noping` override per invocation.
Independent timeout for each of the two ICMP probes; 1ms–10s.

Allow the internal ping-socket pinger, which sends ICMP directly over a Linux ping socket. The kernel grants ping sockets to the groups in the sysctl `net.ipv4.ping_group_range` (for example `net.ipv4.ping_group_range = 1000 9999` covering the operators' groups); widening it is the recommended setup, since the fallback runs a sub-process per gated device.

Allow the external system `ping` executable (found on PATH) as the fallback when ping sockets are refused; less performant because it opens a sub-process per gated device. With both methods disabled while `network.ping-targets` is true the configuration is rejected.
Named transport selector. `default` resolves to system for login; `preferred` resolves to native.
Named transport selector. `default` resolves to system for command; `preferred` resolves to native.
Named transport selector. `default` resolves to native for run; `preferred` also resolves to native.
System-SSH executable name or path. Relative paths resolve from the karvi executable directory.
Preferred compiled-in SSH implementation. Built-in default unavailability is tolerated until selected; an explicit unavailable value is a configuration error.
Include `~/.ssh/config` after compatibility and managed-default blocks; it supplies only still-unset options such as approved bastion routing.

Unified login, command, and run host-key policy: accept-new accepts new keys and rejects changes; secure requires prior enrollment; insecure accepts all keys with warnings. The removed values auto and default are rejected.

The karvi trust store, the one `known_hosts` file both transports trust. `auto` is `<basedir>/known_hosts`: the operator's root under the site's `users` directory, else `~/.local/share/karvi/known_hosts`; an explicit path is taken as given, `~` the home. `config show --explain ssh.known-hosts-file` names the file.
When true, the first changed SSH host key stops new run scheduling while allowing in-flight devices to finish.

The operator's own keys, offered in this order where a platform's `fallback` reaches `keys`: each an absolute path or `~/`, the home the password database names. A file that does not exist is passed over; one that is not the operator's own regular file without group or other access, holds a passphrase, or is hardware-backed is skipped with `operator_key_skipped`.
At least one auth mechanism must remain.
Supports network-device challenge prompts.
0 disables; otherwise 1s–10m.
1–100 when interval nonzero.

The directory of the system transport's control sockets, a private real directory (0700, the operator's). `auto` is `/dev/shm/karvi/<username>/sockets` when the site's scratch root exists, else `<basedir>/socket/ssh`; an absolute path, or one beginning with `~/` (the operator's home), replaces both. A socket's path holds the root, a 16-character name, and OpenSSH's 17-character binding suffix within 107 bytes, so the root may be at most 73 bytes (`control_path_root_too_long` at planning, for a target that runs exec over the system transport). A socket a master killed outright left is swept at the daemon's start and at every job's admission.

Host-key algorithms both SSH transports offer, strongest first; each transport offers the names it implements, filtered to the key types the trust store holds for the device. `ssh-dss`, certificate, and security-key algorithms are refused.
Key exchanges both SSH transports offer, strongest first. `diffie-hellman-group1-sha1` and `diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1` only in an ssh-algorithms-profile.
Ciphers both SSH transports offer, strongest first. AES-192 and AES-128 only in an ssh-algorithms-profile; `3des-cbc`, non-AES CBC, `arcfour`, and `none` are refused.
MACs both SSH transports offer, strongest first. UMAC-128 only in an ssh-algorithms-profile; MD5, truncated, and 64-bit MACs are refused.
0 disables; otherwise 1s–10m.
1–100 when enabled.
1s–12h; caps each command whole over telnet, from the write to the prompt, unless the command is given `--timeout`.
1s–12h; each command's timeout where a session-init profile sets none, which a requested command's `--timeout` replaces for that command.

1s–5m; the first prompt after login and the prompt after each paging command. The system transport awaits the first prompt for `ssh.connect-timeout` plus this value from the start of its `ssh` process; scrapligo-v1 for this value after its handshake.
1s–5m; one privilege level's whole step, from the escalate command to that level's prompt.

0 disables; otherwise 1s–168h. Bounds one device's whole command list, the session-init profile included, from the prepared session; ends it with `device_timeout`. A command's `--timeout` above it is refused at planning.

0–10m, enforced when the plan is drafted. The wait for the prompt after a blind send, a command ending in `\r` sequences or given `--blind-return N`, in place of its command timeout; 0 sends and does not wait. The client's effective value travels in the execution plan, so `--blind-wait` reaches the daemon.
CLI opt-out is explicit.
`serial`, `parallel`, `wave`.
0 means logical CPU count; otherwise 1–4096, the absolute ceiling.
1–4096; hard validation ceiling.

0–4096. The host's cap on device sessions in flight at once, across every job, every operator's daemon, and in-process runs on the host, held as leases in the capacity ledger under `sessions.shared-capacity-root` (across operators where the site made the scratch root with `sudo karvi setup shared`, per operator where it did not); a job's width is also bounded by it. `0` means `min(256, max(32, 8 × CPU))`: 32 on a host of four logical CPUs, 128 on sixteen, 256 from thirty-two up. A site whose devices and AAA carry more sets the figure it wants, 512 or 1024 among them, together with `dispatch.parallel-workers` or `dispatch.wave-max-width` and `dispatch.absolute-max-width` (`docs/SCALE.md`).
10ms–1s; ≤ max.
10ms–5s; ≥ min.

The platform of a device whose platform is not set (a blank inventory row without a source default, or a direct target without `--platform`): a known platform, `cisco_iosxe` as shipped since registry 17, `generic` or empty for `generic`, or the platform a site's network is predominantly.

`fail` refuses an activity whose target set holds an inventory row naming an unknown platform (`platform_unknown`); `warn` runs the device as `platform-resolution.unknown-fallback` with a warning and the notice `platform_unknown_fallback`. Configuration values fail validation whatever this says.
The known platform an unknown inventory row runs as under `on-unknown = "warn"`; not read under `fail`.

The capacity ledger's root. `auto` is `/dev/shm/karvi/capacity`, the ledger every operator on the host shares, where the site's scratch root `/dev/shm/karvi` exists (`sudo karvi setup shared` makes it, at 2770 in the operators' group; a missing `capacity` is made in the root with its bits), else the private `<basedir>/state/capacity`; a shared root present but not usable by the operator (the sticky bit on another's directory, a closed directory or lock file) is passed by for the private one with one warning (`capacity_root_unusable`). The ledger's files take the root's group modes. A path (`~` the operator's home, a relative path from the working directory) replaces the chain, used or refused.
Safe per-UID path.

0 never exits; else 1m–30d. The daemon stops itself, as `daemon stop` would, once this long has passed with no active job, no preparation in progress, and no request but ping and status; checked once a minute. The packaged systemd unit sets 0.
0–60; ≤ normal grace unless normal 0.
64 KiB–64 MiB.
10–10,000; terminal jobs leave memory after finalization.
`auto`: the shared `jobs` tree under `sharedroot` when one exists, else `<basedir>/jobs`; an explicit path is that writable real directory.

Whether the activity keeps a job folder and its files, on every path (`command`, `run --no-daemon`, and a run through the daemon); false, or `--nof`, writes nothing and displays the records from memory or the socket.
Write every device's `output.TARGET.txt`, the session as text; false does not create them. Written from the record in memory, so it does not need `commands.jsonl`.

Write `commands.jsonl`, the records; false does not create it, on every path (records travel over the socket). Without it `job follow` cannot replay the job and a device's text cannot be derived again.
Write `commands.txt`, the rerun's command file (`--cf`); false does not create it.
Write `errors.jsonl`, the records that did not succeed (each is also in `commands.jsonl`); false does not create it.
Write `failed-devices.txt`, the rerun's target file (`--tf`); false does not create it.
Write `manifest.json`, the job as it was accepted; false does not create it.
Write `metrics.json`; false does not create it.

Write `summary.json`; false does not create it, on every path. A finished job without one is `job_orphaned` to a later `job follow` once the daemon has let it go. `karvi-prune` knows a finished job by it; a folder without one is an orphan, removed by age alone once its day, everything in it, and its scoreboard file are older than the retention age. With all eight keys false no job folder is created.

The device name in a file name (`output.NAME.txt`, `crun/NAME`) is the canonical name's first label, lowercased; `false` writes the whole name, lowercased. An address is never cropped: its dots and colons are hyphens. Carried in the plan, so a job's files are named as its invocation said on every path.

The collection directory, one file per device named by the device, of `crun` and of `run` or `command` given `--cd`: `auto` is the shared `crun` tree under `sharedroot` when one exists, else `<basedir>/crun`; an explicit path is resolved as `output.root` is (`~` expanded, a relative path from the working directory). `--cd=PATH` sets it for one invocation, and on `run` and `command` asks for the collection. Carried in the plan.

`0750`, `0755`, or `0770`: the mode of the collection directory when karvi creates it. An existing directory is left as it is in mode, group, and setgid bit; a shared one is made once by the site with `chgrp` and `chmod 2770` or `2775`.
`0640`, `0644`, or `0660`: the mode of each collection file, applied to the temporary before the rename, so the file appears at that mode and takes the directory's group under setgid.

An executable the client runs once a `crun` has ended and its display is printed (never after a `run` or `command` given `--cd`), empty for none: in the collection directory, with the replaced files' names on standard input one per line and the job in `KARVI_JOB_ID`, `KARVI_JOB_DIR` (empty under `--nof`), `KARVI_CRUN_DIRECTORY`, `KARVI_CRUN_REPLACED`, `KARVI_CRUN_KEPT`, and `KARVI_EXIT`; its output goes to karvi's standard error after the display. It runs on the in-process and the daemon path alike, not under `--detach`; a hook that cannot start, exits non-zero, or runs past `crun.after-timeout` is the warning `crun_after_failed`, and the run's exit code stands (docs/COLLECTION.md).
1s–1h. How long `crun.after` may run: on expiry the hook's process group is sent SIGTERM, killed five seconds later if still there, and the warning `crun_after_failed` says it ran past the timeout.
1 KiB–1 GiB; the bound on one command's output, which a command's `--maxbytes` replaces for that command (at most `output.max-job-bytes`).

0–1 GiB, in bytes; the spool threshold per in-flight command: a response is held in memory up to it and spools to a file under `spooldir` from the byte that crosses it. `0` spools every response from its first byte; a value at or above `output.max-command-bytes` means no command spools, since the limit ends a response first, and no rule refuses the pair. The daemon's memory for output is then in flight × (this threshold + a few windows of at most 4 KiB), whatever the responses' sizes.
≥ max command; ≤1 TiB. Counts what is written of the devices' output: the `commands.jsonl` lines and the text blocks of every `output.TARGET.txt`.
0–1 GiB; capacity estimate.

0–1 TiB; 2 GiB by default. The floor every volume an activity writes must keep free after the activity's estimate: under `freecheck = "auto"` it is added once to each volume's sum, under `always` it is the whole ask.
False requires global lock and durability warning.
`auto`, `strip`, `preserve`.
Shared terminal theme: `auto`, `dark`, `light`, or `nocolor`.
Terminal color policy: `auto`, `always`, or `never`. `auto` colours at a terminal unless `NO_COLOR` is set and not empty; `always` and `never` are explicit and `NO_COLOR` does not override them.
Human-facing timestamp pattern. Supports yyyy, yy, MM/month-context mm, dd, hh, minute-context mm, ss, and sss. Stored records remain RFC 3339.

One-line template for the ICMP gate's result of each gated device in text output, before the device's header, styled as the headers are; empty disables it. `<rtt1>` and `<rtt2>` are the two probes' round-trip times, `timeout`, or `error`; `<result>` is `proceeding` or `skipped`. Suppressed by `--quiet`; ICMP error details and the packet-loss notice line appear only under `--debug`.
Color for successful terminal status; default selects the active theme palette.
Color for warning and halted terminal status; default selects the active theme palette.
Color for failed terminal status; default selects the active theme palette.
Color for stale or secondary terminal information; default selects the active theme palette.
Color for changing or emphasized terminal information; default selects the active theme palette.

Color for brackets, punctuation, and element labels such as platform, user, backend, and transport; default is blue under the dark theme and gray under the light theme.
Color for ordinary generated header and footer values; default selects the active theme palette.
Color for generated command border text; default is gray in the built-in themes.
Color for the dash line requested by command or run --border; default is gray in the built-in themes.
One-line login header template; empty disables it.
One-line login footer template; empty disables it.
One-line template naming a recorded login's transcript (`login --record`) before the session, rendered as the login header is; `<transcript>` is the file's path. Empty disables it.

One-line template naming a recorded login's transcript after the session's last output, a failed session included; the same default as `display.record.header`, so the two lines match. Empty disables it.
One-line command header template; empty disables it.

One-line command footer template; empty disables it. <reference-id> remains available for custom templates but is omitted from the default because the activity ID is already present in the artifacts path.
Separator emitted between command outputs. Default is one blank line. Newlines are allowed; `<repeat:TEXT:COUNT>` expands repeated text, for example `<repeat:-:40>\n`.
1–4096. Dash count used by command --border when no header is displayed. A displayed header instead determines the dynamic border length.
When true, emit the configured or dynamic border after the final command. False suppresses the unnecessary trailing separator.
Show the effective device prompt and sent command before each attempted command result in human text output, including device-reported errors.
Per-device header used by run --format text; empty disables it. A failed record still emits an explicit error line.

One-line footer template that ends a run's text display on every path, the daemon follow, --no-daemon, job follow, and a finished job's replay, from the job's summary (its exit, duration, and job folder); empty disables it. Under --format jsonl the summary document is the stream's last line instead, and nothing ends the run on standard error.

One-line template after the footer of a job with a collection (`crun`, or `run` or `command` with `--cd`), on standard output under `--format text` on every path: `<collection>` the absolute collection directory, `<replaced>` and `<kept>` the devices whose files were replaced and kept. Under json and jsonl nothing is printed (the summary carries the collection block). Empty disables it.
Separator emitted between run command records. Default is one blank line. Newlines and `<repeat:TEXT:COUNT>` are supported.
1–4096. Dash count used by run --border when no per-device header is displayed.
When true, emit the configured or dynamic border after the final run command record. False suppresses the trailing separator.
Show the effective device prompt and sent command before each attempted run command result in human text output, including device-reported errors; JSONL remains undecorated.
1–8. Spaces per indentation level for --format json. Compact --format jsonl remains one record per line.
